To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-17 is a weak stimulus of proinflammatory mediator release by lung structural cells, but markedly enhances their responses to secondary stimuli.

IL-17 enhances the IL-8 and the IL-6 responses of human lung epithelial and fibroblast cells to secondary stimuli by reducing IL-8 and/or IL-6 mRNA decay, but is only a weak stimulus of these cytokines.
IL-17 induces IL-8 and -6 hyperresponsiveness in structural lung cells by modulating IL-8 and –6 mRNA degradation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of IL-6 and IL-8 expression in human lung epithelial and fibroblastic cells.
the regulation of the innate immune response of the airway epithelium.
understanding how the immune system regulates inflammation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adaptive immune system, by releasing IL-8 and/or IL-6, modulates the innate immune system by inducing hyperresponsiveness to a secondary stimulus, and thus, the innate immune response.

IL-17 enhances proinflammatory responses to secondary inflammatory mediators by reducing the IL-8 and the IL-6 mRNA turnover in structural lung cells and thus contributes to the pathogenesis of asthma.
IL-17 induces hyperresponsiveness of IL-8- or IL-6-producing structural lung cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-17 induces hyperresponsiveness in lung structural cells, which may be a novel mechanism by which the adaptive immune system contributes to airway inflammation.
IL-17 instructs the structural cells of the lung to become hyperresponsive to inflammatory stimuli.
IL-17 instructs the innate immune response in the lung by enhancing the responsiveness of lung cells to inflammatory stimuli, and thereby contributes to the amplification of inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-17 is an amplifier of the proinflammatory response rather than being a proinflammatory cytokine in itself.
the immune system can modulate the innate immune response in a way that is not only pro- or anti-inflammatory, but also hyperinflammatory.
IL-17 is a weak proinflammatoy stimulus by itself.
